sources.label: WebGPU specification (gpuweb/gpuweb) — §14.2 Immediate Data: GPUBindingCommandsMixin.setImmediates(), GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor.immediateSize, GPUSupportedLimits.maxImmediateSize
gpuweb/gpuweb issue #5118 — Immediates proposal, render-bundle behaviour (linked twice from the page)
MDN — WebGPU API (linked from the page's see-also; carries no immediates coverage, so no dimension relies on it)

outputs.rationale: The spec's setImmediates() definition reads "Returns: undefined": the call records a command and yields no value, and the page's per-draw example consumes none.

errors.rationale: GAP: the page documents no failure behaviour. The cited spec throws an OperationError for a negative or out-of-range contentsSize and invalidates the encoder when rangeOffset is not a multiple of 4 or exceeds maxImmediateSize; #constraints states the alignment and size rules but never their consequence.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page has no security or privacy section, and the ChromeStatus record it cites sets both security_review_status and privacy_review_status to "Not applicable"; the method writes bytes the calling page already holds.

outputs.rationale: A dictionary member read at createPipelineLayout() time returns nothing of its own; the created GPUPipelineLayout is the output and the page documents none of its surface.

errors.rationale: GAP: the page documents no error path for this member. The spec requires the pipeline layout's [[immediateSize]] to be at least the shader's required immediate size and bounds it by maxImmediateSize, neither of which the page states as a failure rule.

lifecycle.rationale: The value is copied once into the immutable pipeline layout and has no lifecycle of its own; the lifetime of the data it sizes is the per-pass scope stated in #constraints.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Sizing a pipeline layout's immediate data range exposes no new origin-visible data, and neither the page nor the cited ChromeStatus record raises a security or privacy consideration for it.

errors.rationale: GAP: the page documents no shader-creation or validation error for immediate variables. The WGSL rules the page omits are the host-shareable-constructible store type, the exclusion of arrays and structures containing array members, and the one-immediate-variable-per-entry-point limit.

securityPrivacy.rationale: An immediate variable is read-only inside the shader and exposes only the bytes the same page wrote through the API; the page documents no security or privacy consideration for the address space.

inputs.rationale: A read-only device limit takes no arguments and has no input contract: it is queried from the adapter or device, never called or written.

outputs.rationale: The row states the value the limit yields, but its number is disputed: see the notes divergence (3) - the spec limits table gives maxImmediateSize a default of 64, the page says "at least 128 bytes guaranteed".

errors.rationale: GAP: the page documents no failure behaviour when a pipeline's immediate size exceeds the limit; the spec invalidates the encoder when rangeOffset + contentsBytes exceeds limits.maxImmediateSize.

lifecycle.rationale: A device limit is fixed for the lifetime of the adapter and device it was queried from and has no creation, mutation or teardown steps of its own.

examples.rationale: Mapped to the pipeline-layout example rather than to #constraints because #constraints holds no <pre><code>: the example is where a byte size the limit bounds is actually chosen (16 bytes = 4 x float32).

securityPrivacy.rationale: Querying this limit reveals only a hardware capability already exposed by WebGPU's other device limits, and the cited ChromeStatus record marks both security and privacy review "Not applicable".

notes:
CAMPAIGN B4 UNIT v150/webgpu-immediates. IDS ADDED (six, all on headings, none on a <section>): the three canonical ids #syntax (h3 "JavaScript: set data per draw"), #browser-support (h2 "browser support") and #see-also (h2 "see also"), plus three supporting ids the inventory needs so that every dimension points at a slice that really contains it: #pipeline-layout (h3 "pipeline layout: declare immediate data range"), #wgsl-immediate (h3 "WGSL shader: read from immediate address space") and #constraints (h2 "constraints"). The h2 "the API" carries NO id on purpose: its section opens immediately with an h3, so a fragment there would resolve to nothing. No code block was added - the page already ships three <pre><code> blocks (pipeline layout, WGSL shader, per-draw JavaScript). Nothing else on the page was changed.

FOUR INVENTORY ROWS AND NO FEWER, because the cited specification declares four distinct developer-facing members with distinct inputs, outputs and failure rules: GPUBindingCommandsMixin.setImmediates(), GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor.immediateSize, GPUSupportedLimits.maxImmediateSize and the WGSL immediate address space. outOfScope CANNOT be used to trim this inventory: that array is validated against the members declared in the page's own #syntax IDL block, and this page's #syntax block is JavaScript, not WebIDL, so any outOfScope entry would match no declared member and fail validation.

SOURCES ARE RESTRICTED TO THE FOUR URLS THE PAGE ALREADY LINKS, because the validator requires the page to link every source an inventory row or dimension cites, and this unit is forbidden from editing the page's citations. The normative WGSL document (https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/wgsl/), the merged proposal (https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/blob/main/proposals/immediate-data.md) and spec PR #5423 (https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/pull/5423) were all read while assessing this page but are NOT listed as sources: the page does not link them, so citing them would red the validator. They are named here and in the unit report instead. The MDN row is listed because the page links it, and is referenced by no dimension because MDN carries no immediates coverage at all.

DIVERGENCES FOUND AGAINST THE CITED SPECIFICATION - REPORTED, NOT ADJUDICATED, AND NOT REPAIRED ON THE PAGE (this unit may not write prose). (1) METHOD NAME: the page writes setImmediateData(offset, data) in the lede, in the #syntax paragraph and in its code example; the spec IDL declares "undefined setImmediates(GPUSize32 rangeOffset, AllowSharedBufferSource data, optional GPUSize64 dataOffset = 0, optional GPUSize64 dataSize)" (#dom-gpubindingcommandsmixin-setimmediates), and the WGSL document says the value "is set via setImmediates commands". The ChromeStatus record's summary still uses the older setImmediateData() spelling, which is where the page's name appears to come from. (2) DESCRIPTOR MEMBER: the page writes immediateDataRangeByteSize: 16; the spec declares "GPUSize32 immediateSize = 0" in GPUPipelineLayoutDescriptor (#dom-gpupipelinelayoutdescriptor-immediatesize). (3) DEVICE LIMIT NAME AND VALUE: the page's #constraints row reads "Defined by the device limit maxImmediateDataRangeByteSize (at least 128 bytes guaranteed)"; the spec declares "readonly attribute unsigned long maxImmediateSize" on GPUSupportedLimits and its limits table row reads "maxImmediateSize | GPUSize32 | maximum | 64 | The maximum size, in bytes, of immediate data range used in a pipeline. Note: 64 bytes is the size of a 4x4 matrix of f32 values."; the merged proposal's limits table also gives maxImmediateSize a default of 64 ("64 bytes is the sizeof(mat4x4)"), and the WGSL limits table gives the matching standalone limit 64. No source read for this assessment supports 128. (4) ARITY: the page shows a two-argument setImmediateData(offset, data); the spec method takes rangeOffset, data and the optional dataOffset and dataSize. (5) TYPES ROW: the page's #constraints row reads "Host-shareable structs only; cannot reference textures or samplers"; the WGSL document reads "A variable in the immediate address space is an immediate data variable. Its store type must be a host-shareable constructible type, excluding arrays and structures that contain array members", and the merged proposal's own sample declares "var<immediate> b : i32;", i.e. a scalar, not a struct. (6) SUPPORT-TABLE PROVENANCE: the page's Firefox and Safari cells read "Not yet; following the WebGPU spec" cited to "chromestatus.com browser positions, May 2026"; the ChromeStatus API record (accurate_as_of 2026-06-02) carries ff_views 3 and safari_views 3, which chromium-dashboard's core_enums maps to PUBLIC_SUPPORT = 'Positive' for both Gecko and WebKit. The record's own interop note adds that the feature "has been approved in W3C GPU for the Web WG meetings including participants from WebKit and Firefox". (7) SHIPMENT STATUS - CHECKED, AND NOT A DIVERGENCE: the page's at-a-glance rows read "Shipped in Chrome 150" and "Status: Enabled by default". The single-feature API record looked contradictory (browsers.chrome.desktop/android/webview are all 150, yet status.text reads "Proposed" and is_released is false), so the ChromeStatus milestone listing was fetched too: https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features?milestone=150 files feature 5199437611794432 in the "Enabled by default" bucket (fetched 2026-10-07), which supports both rows. The record's status.text is a lagging field rather than a contradiction of the page, and no change is proposed for it. Item 6 is likewise provenance imprecision rather than a hard contradiction - "Not yet" is consistent with a vendor position that is Positive but unshipped - but the recorded position token itself is absent from the page.

GAPS RECORDED AS not-applicable WITH THE GAP NAMED (missing is forbidden and would red the validator): ERRORS is not-applicable on all four rows because the page documents no failure behaviour anywhere, while the cited spec does - setImmediates() throws an OperationError on the content timeline when contentsSize >= 0 fails, when dataOffset + contentsSize > dataElementCount, or when contentsSize in bytes is not a multiple of 4, and it invalidates the encoder on the device timeline when rangeOffset is not a multiple of 4 or when rangeOffset + contentsBytes exceeds limits.maxImmediateSize; the spec also requires every accessible immediate slot to have been set before a draw or dispatch. The page's #constraints table states the 4-byte alignment and size rules but never says what happens when they are broken. SECURITYPRIVACY is not-applicable on all four rows: the page has no security or privacy section, and the ChromeStatus record it cites sets security_review_status and privacy_review_status to "Not applicable". OUTPUTS is not-applicable on the descriptor-member row (a dictionary member has no return value of its own) and on the method row (the spec's setImmediates() dfn reads "Returns: undefined", and the page's example consumes no value). INPUTS and LIFECYCLE are not-applicable on the device-limit row (a read-only limit is queried, takes no arguments, and is fixed for the adapter's lifetime) and LIFECYCLE is not-applicable on the descriptor-member row (the value is copied once into the immutable pipeline layout).

CITATION GAPS LEFT ON THE PAGE BECAUSE THIS UNIT MAY NOT EDIT PROSE: the label "gpuweb spec PR #5423" in the #syntax citation is unlinked (the ChromeStatus record's spec_link and initial_public_proposal_url are both https://github.com/gpuweb/gpuweb/pull/5423); the #browser-support citation "chromestatus.com browser positions, May 2026" is plain text with no link; and the normative WGSL document that defines the immediate address space is not linked from the page at all.
